subject: SIG follow-up — crypto escrow & data residency for OpaQuest
messages:
From: Ethan Lewis <ethan.lewis@opaquest.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: security@opaquest.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: SIG-lite items — escrowed keys & EU residency

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the SIG-lite draft you shared last week. Our procurement team is comfortable with most answers, but our security reviewers flagged two items they need clarifying before we can finalize:

1) Key escrow / crypto custody: we need to understand whether any of Redwood's subprocessors hold long-term copies of customer encryption keys or plaintext artifacts. If so, what controls and access procedures exist? A diagram of KMS flows would be ideal.

2) Data residency for EU customers: OpaQuest operates EU-only tenants and requires confirmation that any subprocessor handling inference artifacts for EU tenants is physically located in the EU or covered by SCCs + documented cross-border safeguards. Please provide the list of subprocessors that may see model inputs/outputs for EU-hosted tenants and their residency.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide: (a) a KMS flow diagram and short explanation of escrow policies, and (b) a CSV roster of subprocessors with residency and data handling role (storage/compute/telemetry)?

We appreciate a response by EOD tomorrow if possible; our renewal is timing-sensitive.

Best,
Ethan

--
Ethan Lewis
Head of Security, OpaQuest
security@opaquest.com

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Lewis <ethan.lewis@opaquest.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SIG-lite items — escrowed keys & EU residency

Ethan — thanks for the clear asks. Short answer up front: we do not escrow long-term customer encryption keys with external subprocessors; keys are customer-managed where required and our infrastructure KMS paths are scoped per account, with limited operator access. That said, some subprocessors (e.g., managed logging and telemetry vendors) may receive derivative telemetry or aggregated usage metrics — not plaintext customer payloads — unless a customer explicitly configures log export.

We'll produce: 1) a KMS/keyflow diagram (annotated) and a short bullets doc describing escrow exceptions and operator access controls; 2) a CSV roster of subprocessors with columns for name, role, region residency, and whether they may handle model input/output.

Marissa and Ben — looping you in to assemble the subproc roster and the annotated keyflow. Marissa can you pull the latest roster (ensure we mark EU-resident compute/storage partners) and Ben can validate the KMS diagram / operator access language.

Ethan — I expect to get the packaged evidence to you by EOD tomorrow. If you need a written attestation for procurement, we can draft a short statement.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: SIG-lite items — escrowed keys & EU residency

Ethan — thanks for the patience. Please find our responses and the requested artifacts attached. Summary up front:

1) Key escrow / crypto custody
- Redwood does not escrow customer-managed long-term data encryption keys with any third party. Customers may opt for customer-managed keys (CMKs) in their own KMS; Redwood will accept wrapped keys or use an API to integrate with customer KMS.
- For platform operations, Redwood uses a central service-managed KMS for ephemeral application keys. Access to plaintext keys is restricted to a small, role-based operator group and requires just-in-time (JIT) privileged session approval and audit logging.
- Exceptions: For disaster-recovery onboarding (rare, documented), a short-lived recovery key may be stored encrypted with a FIPS-validated HSM provided by a third-party key custodian; such events are contractually scoped and require documented customer approval.

2) Subprocessor residency & handling (CSV attached)
- Attached: subprocessor_roster_2026-07.csv (redacted column: ContactEmail). Columns: Name, Role, Region, MayHandlePayload, ContractualSCCs, Notes.
- EU compute/storage partners that may process EU tenant inputs are clearly marked. All cross-border transfers are controlled via SCCs (customers may request DPA addenda for extra controls).

Attachments included (redacted for external delivery):
- sig-lite-answers.pdf (SIG-lite Q&A with callouts)
- subprocessor_roster_2026-07.csv (redacted)
- kms-keyflow-annotated.png (KMS flow diagram with operator-control annotations)

If you would like a signed attestation for procurement, we can provide a short letter on Redwood letterhead confirming the points above and listing the EU-resident subprocessors. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the diagram.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Manager, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
